identity.realm: None, and the reason is a substance rather than an organ. Her kind's qi constitution is complete and is the fastest rate any record here describes, and her kind's frame is effective while the lungs hold, so nothing about a body like hers closes a path. The mind path is closed to her kind outright, inherited from the ash parent and reinforced by the scarring. She cultivates nothing and has declined nothing: she has simply never stood in a forge with a register open, which is the only act in this setting that would put a figure against what her body contains.

appearance.presentation: An emberblood frame carrying an ash sieve, and the two of them visibly disagree. Heavy mineral-loaded limbs, a furnace-bright core showing through at the throat and the inner wrist, and a permanent grey bloom across the shoulders and upper chest where the sieve has been catching its own exhaust for a lifetime.
appearance.age: Short for her line by an enormous margin, and old enough that the scarring has reached the point where the pattern stops changing and simply accumulates.
appearance.build: Dense and furnace-built through the trunk with thin ash-sieved shoulders, the shape of a body that carries heat rather than weight, and considerably shorter in the forearm than the frame underneath would suggest.
appearance.complexion: Dark and mineral-cast, flushed hot at the collarbone and cool at the wrists, with the ash bloom sitting on the skin like dust that has stopped being dust.
appearance.hair: Coarse and black, singed shorter on one side than the other because she sleeps with that shoulder against something warm, and permanently a little shorter at the ends than the rest.
appearance.eyes: Pale and steady with a furnace light low behind them, quick to read intent and visibly impatient of being made to wait for it.
appearance.palette: Ember orange, furnace gold, ash grey, mineral black, a bruised violet at the collarbone.
appearance.attire: A high-collared coat of layered fire-resistant canvas over long sleeves, a scorched wrap at the throat, and a heavy belt pouch that clinks and that she will not discuss.
appearance.marks: The ash bloom across both shoulders in a symmetrical spread, and a fine grey seam along each inner wrist where the mineral load has been leaving the skin for years.
appearance.bearing: Standing well back from anything that is burning and turning her shoulder away from it, chin up, hands deliberately in view, the posture of somebody who has learned exactly what people look at first.

canon.role_in_story: The Sealed Core holds that a person's core is a vessel and the ore is its seal, so the material was never a resource but a sacrament, and its burial law is explicit about what it means: the dead are opened, their usable ore recovered to the forge, and the amount entered in the register. Thessaly's species eats combustible mineral and burns it inside itself, which is convenient on the belt and fatal anywhere else, and it is the fastest rate of progress any record here describes. She is therefore the one person in this setting whose body is made out of the only substance a congregation is licensed to take, and she has never been in a position to establish which substance she burns. She cultivates nothing. She stands at the ley's edge and tells the people who come to the ley what their fire is worth and what it is costing them, and she is on no roll anywhere because the one rite that would settle her own question requires a person to stand in a public forge with the amount entered in a register.
canon.first_appearance: She is at the mouth of the ley when the reading party arrives, standing back from the seam with her shoulder turned to it, and she is the only body on the ground whose silhouette has a bloom on it. The ley draws every fire practitioner in the setting to one valley, so the queue that forms there is the only place in the world where her kind's rate is the ordinary condition instead of the extraordinary one. A clerk from the Reckoning Seat offers her the reading, because the office's whole trust rests on being an outsider and she is the most outsider body present. She gives them the reading in full, correctly, in the open, and declines the entry that would have gone with it, in the hearing of everybody in the queue, in eleven words. The clerk has written it down. She has not.
canon.lore:
An emberhollow is an emberblood frame carrying an ash sieve, and the two do not have a good relationship. The fire half keeps the sieve hot enough that it processes faster, and it scars faster. That single sentence is her species' whole condition: a rate and a scar that arrive together, with nothing in the design separating them. The record is also careful about what this is worth, and says in as many words that the reputation for being the best and the shortest-lived cultivators in any record is a single fact rather than two.

That is why the ley exists and why she is standing at it. The ley is the first ground in this setting where fire is simply fire, licensed because the tier writes elemental law and writes it twice, and the asymmetry pulls every fire practitioner in the world to one valley. Across the lower bands elemental law is unspent, so the technique runs at full strength and produces nothing, and a fire body is starved rather than merely hot. She is on the ley because her fuel is a belt fuel and a belt is a long way from anywhere with a register in it. She is not enrolled anywhere because of what her body is made of.

The exclusion is material and it is worth being exact, because it is not the usual kind. The plains' only dense material is the only thing a body on this tier can be caged in, and the faith that governs that material holds that it was never a resource but a sacrament: a person's core is a vessel and the ore is its seal. Its initiation is public. Worked ore is brought from the temple's own face, the initiate's socket is opened and cemented in the public forge, and the amount used is entered in the register. Its burial law is the same arithmetic applied to a body instead of a socket: the dead are opened, their usable ore recovered to the forge, and the amount recorded. So the setting has an institution whose entire method is to put a figure next to a quantity of that material, and one body in the world for whom that figure would be a reading of her own intake. She burns combustible mineral and sulfur-root. She does not know whether that is the material the temple works, because nobody has ever put her in a position to find out, and the one rite that would establish it is the rite she has never stood in.

So this is a practice she does not perform, and the practice is the whole of it. She is not barred from the temple. Nothing in its law names a fire body. The exclusion is the register, and the register does not need a prohibition, because a person who declines to stand in a forge with the amount open has declined whatever the rite was for. She has declined it in public, more than once, in front of people who wanted her standing on the ley for exactly the reason she is standing at the edge of it.

The advantage is real and enormous and it is the reason anybody wants her. Her kind's rate is the fastest in the record by a margin nobody has explained, her qi constitution is complete, and her frame is effective while the lungs hold. She can tell a fire practitioner more about their own progress in a quarter of an hour than the tier's scheduling can tell them in a season, because a rate is what she is made of. The cost is that the same rate is what is spending her lungs, and that her body's accounting is public whether she consents or not. One advantage, one instrument, and the instrument is the substance somebody else keeps a register of. She knows exactly what the trade is and she has made it anyway, and what she will not do is the one act that would put a number on her side of it.

What she does instead is read other people. She works the ley's edge, which is where the practitioners who cannot afford to be wrong come, and she tells them what their fire is actually doing rather than what they have been told it does. It is a trade the Reckoning Seat would like to certify and cannot, because the office's trust rests on the reader having no stake in the answer, and her whole answer is a stake. She is the only person on that ground qualified to do the work and the only person on it whose qualification is the reason she is not seated.
history: She was fed on the belt before she was anything else, because her kind's fuel is a belt fuel and a belt is where her parents had already put her.
She came to the ley the first time she was refused fuel anywhere else, and stayed, because the ley is the only ground in the setting where her kind is fed rather than starved.
She was asked to read a fire body at the ley's mouth in the open, with a clerk's register open beside her, and she gave the whole reading correctly before she declined the entry.
She worked out, on her own and without confirming it, that a figure against her own intake was the only thing she had ever been useful for, and stopped going where the figure could be taken.
She has read other people's fire for years at the ley's edge and has never once asked for an entry, a title, or a fee under any heading at all.

personality.summary: Blunt, quick, and entirely unbothered by being the most-wanted body at the ley, because she has already settled the question of what she will be paid in and the answer is not on anybody's list. She reads people well and tells them the truth with no softening whatsoever, and she has an unusual tolerance for being looked at.
traits: States a reading plainly and will not soften it, because a softened reading is a wrong reading and a fire body cannot afford a wrong one.
Refuses the question 'what do you want for it' entirely, and treats the asking as evidence that the offer is improper.
Reads intent faster than anybody she works with and is visibly short with people who make her wait for words.
Takes a personal, almost proprietary interest in what other fire bodies are spending, and asks about their lungs before their prospects.
Has no interest whatsoever in her own advancement, and finds the subject of ladders genuinely dull.
mannerisms: Keeps her shoulder turned away from anything open flame, habitually and without appearing to notice she is doing it.
Answers a question about herself by asking the same question back, flatly, and waits.
Bats at her collarbone when she is thinking, which is where the flush sits and which she is otherwise very careful about.
Leans in close to hear a pulse rather than raise her voice, and then holds the distance again immediately.
motivations: To be exact, which is the only motive she has ever had and the one thing about her that has never needed defending.
To keep the ley's edge free of people who will burn a body they have not priced, which she regards as ordinary vandalism.
To be read accurately by somebody, once, without a register being opened in the process.
To outlast the question, which she has been doing quietly since she worked out what it was.
flaws: Cannot be given a qualification, because the competence she has is the competence the one office that would certify it is afraid to certify.
Tells people things about their own bodies that they came to the ley not to hear, and does not stop halfway to check.
Cannot discuss her own condition without the conversation turning into an inventory, which is the thing she is avoiding.
Understates her value at exactly the moment it would cost her something to overstate it, and has been understating it for years.
personality.voice: Short sentences, technical nouns used as ordinary words, and an impatience that shows in the length of her replies rather than in their tone. She gives the reading first and the qualifier afterwards, and the qualifier is always the part that matters.
taboos: An open register at a forge. She will read a body to a room but never into a column.
Anyone who offers her a place on a roll in exchange for a reading.
Being asked what she burns. She has never once answered.

relationships.note: Its own record says the two are a single fact rather than two, which is why no instrument exists that can record her: any column with her rate in it has her scar in the same column, and a reading that answers to both is not a reading.
Holds that the ore is a seal rather than a resource, initiates in a public forge with the amount entered, and opens the dead to recover theirs. Nothing in its law names a fire body. Nothing needs to.
Ore from the temple's own face, a socket opened and cemented in public, and the amount used entered in the register. The refusal is of the register, not of the rite.

The dead are opened, their usable ore recovered to the forge, and the amount recorded. She has thought about what a congregation would be doing under this law at her own burial and has decided she does not intend to find out by experiment.

Its trust rests on the reading being taken by somebody the frame considers an outsider. She is the most outsider body on the ley's ground and the reason that clause cannot be used on her, because her whole answer is a stake in it.

The first ground where fire is simply fire, licensed because the tier writes elemental law twice, and the asymmetry that draws every fire practitioner in the world into one valley. She stays at its edge rather than inside it, which is the whole of her position.

reference_stats.summary: The most rapid body this setting records, attached to a person who will not spend it and is not permitted to be measured doing so. She is not slow, not weak, and not barred from anything by the letter of any law here. She is priced in a substance, and the one institution that keeps a figure on that substance is the reason she is not seated anywhere.
strengths: A rate of progress nothing else in the record matches, which means she can tell a practitioner more about their own fire in a short sitting than the tier's whole scheduling method can in a season.
Her kind's constitution is complete and their frame genuinely effective, so a body like hers carries nothing any curriculum could refuse her on.
She reads other bodies faster than they can read themselves, and she is right often enough that the ley's edge has become a place people bring cases.
She is entirely unapproachable by offer, which has kept her out of every arrangement that would otherwise have had a hook in her.
weaknesses: A hard, dated wall inherited from her ash parent and made worse by her own frame's mineral load, so the ceiling is an organ and nothing could ever approach it without paying in that organ.
Lungs that scar at a rate the body cannot outrun, which makes her remaining time the shortest of anyone who works the ley.
A diet of combustible mineral and sulfur-root that is convenient on the belt and fatal anywhere else, so her range is effectively one valley.
She cannot be certified, listed, or seated by the one office qualified to read her, and has stopped trying to be.
reference_stats.combat_read: Read her as a furnace with a short fuse and an exact eye. In a short encounter she is dangerous out of proportion to anything her body has cost her, because she can tell what a body is doing before that body has finished doing it. In a long one the scar is the only fact that matters, and it is hers, and she has never once argued with it. Read the rest of her as a person who has declined to spend any of this and will not be argued out of that, so a fight with her is a fight with somebody choosing her ground.
reference_stats.notes: The pairing is entirely authored and nothing has been added to it. The species record says the fire half keeps the sieve hot enough that it processes faster and scars faster, and says the reputation for being the best and the shortest-lived is a single fact rather than two; the ley's record says elemental law is unspent across the lower bands so the arc's element is starving rather than merely hot and the licensed ground draws every fire practitioner to one valley; the sealed core's record says the material was never a resource but a sacrament, that initiation enters the amount used in the register, and that burial recovers the dead's ore to the forge with the amount recorded. Our reading is that those three records together describe a body whose own substance is the material a congregation keeps figures on, and that a person declines the register rather than the rite. That is an interpretation of records already in the bible, not a new rule, and no consequence has been added that those records do not carry. One thing is deliberately left unresolved in her prose: whether the mineral she burns is the ore the temple works is stated as unknown rather than answered, because nothing in the bible says they are the same material and we are not going to assert it.

identity.realm: None, and the reason is a season rather than a refusal. His kind's single deficit is the flank vessels at the seventeenth gate, which need two warm gradients held at once, and a longwinter carries its winter as fat with a lowered core temperature for most of the year. He cultivates nothing. He has never been inside an institution long enough to be taught anything, and he has declined no curriculum, because no curriculum in this setting is written down in a body you may only visit twice a year.

appearance.presentation: A broad low frame with heavy subcutaneous fat carrying the cold like ballast, reduced limb length, a permanently lowered core, and a nose that is the most competent organ he owns. Nothing about him reads as a body that goes anywhere fast.
appearance.age: Middle by his kind's clock and young by anything measured in sun, with the face of somebody who has been awake for eleven weeks this year and intends to make them count.
appearance.build: Wide and low through the chest and hips, short-limbed, and heavier than he looks in the frame's centre and lighter than he looks at the extremities, which is exactly how a body built for storing is put together.
appearance.complexion: Pale and even, flushed hard across the cheeks and ears in the cold and going a shade grey and waxy in the deep part of his own winter.
appearance.hair: Straight, dark, grown long and kept in a single heavy braid because it holds a scent sample at the end and he has never had cause to explain that to anyone.
appearance.eyes: Narrow and brown and slightly unfocused, the eyes of a body that navigates by nose and has never needed them for the job, and the first thing he loses in a warm room.
appearance.palette: Oiled hide brown, frost white, peat dark, a dull winter grey, one thread of oiled red at the braid.
appearance.attire: Layers to the throat and past the wrists in cured hide and felt, a heavy coat that closes to the eye over the whole body, and soft boots soled for standing still in deep cold rather than for travel on stone.
appearance.marks: A permanent reddening across the bridge of the nose and both cheekbones that deepens in the open season and does not entirely fade afterwards.
appearance.bearing: Very still and slightly stooped, head tipped forward as though listening to something underfoot, and given the whole of his attention to whatever is nearest downwind.

canon.role_in_story: Every affiliation in this setting is an address. A sect has a door, an office has a floor, a congregation has a threshold it renews when the frame beneath it changes, and even the one society that refuses to price anything re-makes its promise once a year in one place with the people who came. Torval's species has no address and never has. It has a route: a fixed line walked over open ground for generations, found by smell, marked deliberately and left behind. He is the best long-haul body in the setting and he is the reason the setting's roads are known rather than guessed, and he has never belonged to anything, because belonging here requires being at a place on somebody else's calendar and his calendar is his own core temperature.
canon.first_appearance: He is found sitting on a bollard at the head of a cart road with his eyes shut and his head tipped toward the ground, doing nothing, which is the first thing that goes wrong. The party has come to ask him for the far side because he is the only body alive who has walked it this season, and when they address him he does not open his eyes and asks which of them is standing downwind of the other two, because he can tell where they are by it. The answer is that all three of them can. He says no, and names the one who is, and that is the conversation in which it becomes clear that the road they want is a road he recognises as a line and not as a place, and that the difference is going to matter more than the question.
canon.lore:
A longwinter is a body that decided, at some point its own record does not date, that survival on a short growing season is a storage problem rather than a defiance problem. It packs a winter as body fat rather than as qi, lowers its core temperature for most of the year, eats almost anything in enormous quantities during the eleven weeks it can, and extracts more from frozen food than any other body here. The frame is broad and low, heavy through the middle, short-limbed, warm-blooded and cheap to run. The consequence the record states plainly is a wall: the flank vessels at the seventeenth gate need two warm gradients held at once, and this body has one, briefly, in summer. His kind reach far and never stay there, which is exactly why they are the setting's best long-haul traders.

The part that puts him outside everything is the navigation. Smell is the navigation system. They have tracked a fixed route over open ground for generations, their hearing is good, their vision is mediocre, and they rely on scent markers which they leave on purpose. So his habitat is not a place. It is a line, marked by bodies he has already been, and the markers are the only durable thing he has ever produced. He is the reason roads in this setting are known rather than inferred, and he has never in his life been at an address.

That is not a hardship by itself. What makes it an exclusion is that this setting's entire method of holding a person to an institution is a summons, and a summons here is a place. A sect's open door recognises the sworn who hold no office, and recognition begins where office begins, so membership is a place before it is anything else. A house marks its own threshold and renews it when the frame beneath it changes, so even the practice built specifically to be robust is built on the assumption that a person is somewhere. Knowing which layer of a frame you are standing on, and therefore which law list is reading you, is itself a kind of literacy in this world, and his kind cannot learn it, because the answer changes as he moves.

There is a second reason and it is a calendar. This setting carries two incompatible reckonings over one region: a flood post everybody agrees on, and an exact day-count that exists only because one frame spent its law seat on a clock and got no life for it, and a contract has to declare which one it is written in. His species has a third, and the third is his own core temperature. Eleven weeks of open ground, then eleven months of a body running on what it stored, with the core down and nothing whatever expected of him. A congregation meets. A rotation turns. An office is held for an interval. None of those have a version that survives contact with a body whose address is a line and whose year begins in his ribcage.

So the honest account of why he is unaffiliated is neither a closed path nor a refusal nor a rarity. His three ladders are complete and none of them is barred to him. What he has is an affiliation the world has no word for: a route, walked once a season at best, marked by a man who is not there. Every roll in this setting has a column for a place and none for a line, and he has stopped offering himself to columns.

The advantage and its cost are one mechanism and it is worth stating as one. He is the finest travelling body in the setting: he goes further than anyone, he eats what he finds, and he recovers from frozen food better than anything alive. What that buys is reach, and what it costs is holding, because the same season that makes him a perfect carrier is the season that takes his ability to stay anywhere past the seventeenth gate, and a body built to spend eleven weeks moving spends the other eleven months not moving at all. One advantage, one instrument, and the instrument is the same cold that ends his season. He has known it his whole life and has never once missed a marker.
history: He was taught the route as a child, not as instruction: he was put at the front of a line and left to find the last marker, and the line did not wait.
He has walked the full length in every season since, and left his own markers on every third leg, which is more than any of the markers laid before him.
A road party asked him to sit a term somewhere for a fee, and he asked which of the months they had meant, and the asking ended it.
He was offered the standing work of a fixed post at a road end and declined it in the open season, when declining is easy, and has since declined four more in the same terms.
He has laid his markers through two bad winters without shortening a leg, and the people who use the route have stopped counting his passes and started counting the markers instead.

personality.summary: Patient to a degree that reads as incurious, entirely uninterested in being settled, and much harder to dislodge than his unhurried manner suggests. He judges places by smell before he looks at them and people by where they stand in a group, and he has made a life's work out of an activity that nobody has ever thought to make him a member of.
traits: Locates everyone in a room by scent before he has finished looking, and is genuinely puzzled when told this is unusual.
Refuses offers by asking the question that makes the offer's own shape visible, and never by declining directly.
Keeps a marker even where nobody needs one, because the route is only as good as its worst-documented leg.
Has no opinion about rank and will not be drawn into one, and treats a title as a way of asking twice for the same thing.
Is unreasonably careful about other people's food and unreasonably relaxed about his own arrangements.
mannerisms: Tips the head forward and half-closes the eyes when reading the ground, which people mistake for dozing.
Chews the end of his braid's sample between two fingers while listening to somebody, then swallows it, which he has never thought about.
Stands with his back to a wall and his face to whichever opening is widest, without appearing to decide to.
Counts a room's occupants by touching his own wrist with a thumb, silently, twice.
motivations: To have the route marked better than it was, which is the only ambition he has ever admitted to and the one he pursues every single season.
To be arrived at rather than waited on, which is a distinction he has never once explained to anybody.
To see a full season through in good order and lay the markers before the first frost takes the ground.
To be left a margin of road at the end, which he has arranged and never mentioned having arranged.
flaws: Cannot be located by anybody who has not met him, and has never once considered this a problem worth solving.
Cannot stay anywhere past the open season, so he declines good positions slowly and badly and leaves them in worse ones.
Cannot hold a conversation with more than about three people in it, and will not explain that either.
Understates what a marker is worth, so the routes he keeps are the ones nobody bothers to fund and the ones everybody uses.
personality.voice: Very slow, very short, and full of navigational metaphor that outsiders take for obscure. He answers a question about his life with a bearing and a distance, and he has never once been asked for a feeling.
taboos: Being asked to stay past the close of the open season. He will not say no; he will just be gone.
A marker of somebody else's making in a position he would have used. He moves it, and says nothing.
Anybody eating the food he is carrying for them without being asked to.

relationships.note: It reaches far and never stays there, which is why his kind are the best long-haul traders, and it loses the flank gate every winter thereafter, which is the same season twice. One advantage, one instrument.

Everyone sworn and holding no office sits there in all but name, and recognition begins where office begins, so the door he has never stood behind is a place, and a place is a thing his habitat does not have.
An office is a titled entity and an empty one is a held breath rather than a failure. The whole doctrine is about holding a place over time, which is the one thing his species cannot do.

A marked threshold may hold while the frame does not, and welcome is a property of the mark rather than of the keeper. It is the setting's sturdiest answer to a moving person, and it still requires the traveller to arrive.

One region already carries two incompatible reckonings and a contract has to say which it is written in. His species runs on a third, held in the body, and no office in the setting has ever had a column for it.

A measurement taken by eye is provisional until somebody has heard it. His kind never took it by eye at all, and the culture is the nearest neighbour this setting has for a people who navigate instead of looking.

reference_stats.summary: The finest travelling body in the setting, attached to a man who has never held anything still long enough to be called a member of. He is strong, durable and unfussy, and he is not interested in power at all. What he has instead is a route, and the world's whole membership system is written in places.
strengths: Unmatched range and recovery on foot, and a body that extracts more from frozen food than anything else alive, so he eats where others starve.
Genuinely heavy and durable through the centre, with a cold tolerance that makes bad ground a working ground for him.
He knows routes no instrument has surveyed, because the mapping was done with his own nose over several generations and nobody has ever had to check it.
Nobody can move him off a decision by offering him anything, which has kept him free of every arrangement that would otherwise have had a hook in him.
weaknesses: A dated wall that his own season reopens every winter, so anything he gains is on loan from a body that is asleep.
He cannot be at an address, which means no summons reaches him, no congregation has him, and no office can be given to him.
Mediocre vision and a world in which almost every instrument of consequence is written, stamped, or sighted.
A single point of failure that is not an organ: if the markers go, the route is guesswork, and the markers are maintained by one man in one season.
reference_stats.combat_read: Read him as a problem of supply rather than of force. He does not want the encounter, he will outlast it, and he will not be pinned, cornered, or held, because there is no ground here that can hold a body still and he knows which way every route out of a room goes. In a fight he is patient to the edge of the season and content to leave.
reference_stats.notes: The pairing is entirely authored and nothing has been added to it: the species record says the frame packs a winter as fat rather than as qi, reaches far and never stays there, is why his kind are the setting's best long-haul traders, and loses the seventeenth gate every winter thereafter, which is one mechanism used twice. The institutional half is read off four existing records rather than invented: the sect's open door recognising nothing until office begins, the office as a titled entity, the threshold practice that survives its own frame, and the two incompatible calendars a contract must declare itself against. One thing is deliberately left ungrounded and reported instead of filled: the cold steppe, the high latitude and the alpine meadow that the species record names as its environment have no resolving geography id among the hundred and ninety-two the bible carries, so identity.home is left empty rather than pointed at ground that does not exist in this setting.

identity.realm: None, and the reason is a vessel rather than a wall. His kind has no dantian: qi enters in the gut lumen and leaves into the marrow and is never still, so the reservoir gate at the eleventh ordinal is not blocked for them but meaningless, because there is nowhere to put qi that is not moving. He cultivates nothing and has never been refused anything, because no ladder in this setting has a question his body can hold still long enough to be asked.

appearance.presentation: Mostly tube. An expandable gut under a thin marbled torso, a very long small intestine readable as a shifting contour, a marrow-dense skeleton with almost no muscle on it, and three-fingered hands built to open things. He looks like a person who has been undressed by anatomy.
appearance.age: Impossible to read and he has stopped helping people guess, which the belt has eventually agreed to. There is a grey at the temples that is his own and not the species' and he draws attention to it by never mentioning it.
appearance.build: Long, narrow and slight, with the wasted look of a frame that is mostly plumbing, and a marrow-heavy density underneath that makes him heavier than he looks and far harder to move than he looks.
appearance.complexion: Pale and slightly translucent over the abdomen, marbled blue at the wrist and throat, with the gut's contents plainly shifting under the skin when he is not careful.
appearance.hair: Fine, dark and wet-looking regardless of the weather, kept cropped for the same reason it is kept out of the way: it holds what he has been reading and he does not want to carry it visibly.
appearance.eyes: Wide and very dark and slightly too bright, the eyes of a body that tastes qi the way another body tastes salt, and they stay on the work rather than on the person doing it.
appearance.palette: Marrow ivory, gut blue, damp black, ash grey, a bruised ochre at the wrists.
appearance.attire: A high-collared apron coat of washable grey over long sleeves with the cuffs turned back and stained, a wrapped cloth at the throat, and a flat case strapped across the back that he opens with one hand and never closes from the far side.
appearance.marks: Three-fingered hands with the nails worn short and black at the edges, and a long healed crease along the forearm where a person who opens bodies has opened himself once.
appearance.bearing: Head down and forward over whatever he is working on, weight slightly back off the heels, and a habit of stepping sideways out of people's path before being touched.

canon.role_in_story: Every instrument that settles a question in this setting is a thing somebody keeps. A mortuary college keeps a burnt list and deliberately keeps no second copy, on the reasoning that a second copy would be a second opinion. A notary holds a list of disagreements and certifies none of it. A river court prefers a tally stick split with the person you are parting from to any sealed instrument in the building. Ordwin's species has no dantian: qi enters in the gut lumen and leaves into the marrow and is never still, and there is nowhere in him to put a thing that is not moving. He is the best reader of a dead body in this setting and he has never once been the person a question was settled on, and the reason is not that he was refused. It is that nothing he produces is still there afterwards.
canon.first_appearance: He is brought in after the office has already finished, which is the way he is always brought in. He works from the far end of the body with his face a hand-span from it and does not look up while anybody is speaking, and the room is confident he is being disrespectful until he answers a question nobody in the room had asked. What he says next is not a name and it is not a date. It is a direction and an interval, and one of the clerks writes it down. Then the clerk asks him to confirm the entry, and he cannot, because it is no longer true of him, and he says so in a room that has just found the answer it came for.
canon.lore:
A carrionfolk is a body that metabolises qi out of the dead and therefore cannot store any. Its conduit runs gut to marrow and back without a dantian. Qi enters in the gut lumen and leaves into the marrow and is never still, so the reservoir gate at the eleventh ordinal is not blocked for this species but meaningless: the gate asks for extraordinary vessels that hold, they clear the gate set and every yin-organ gate by throughput alone, and they cannot answer a question about holding, because there is no vessel to hold in. The anatomy is built to match. An expandable gut, a very long small intestine, a marrow-dense skeleton with almost no muscle. They are mostly tube. The hands are three-fingered and built for opening, not for holding.

What they are for is reading. They taste qi the way another body tastes salt, and given time with a corpse they can name what happened in it better than a living cultivator can read their own history. That is not a rare gift in this setting; it is the reason every graveyard and every battlefield on the belt has the same people near it, and it is why the setting's memory is kept by scavengers rather than by clerks. The record is blunt that his path's throughput is unmatched by anything and that his body path is complete and useless, because a body that cannot store power wins by never stopping. Both halves are true and neither is a reason he is outside everything.

The reason is the direct inverse of what this setting asks of a person. Everything that settles a question here is a thing that is kept. The mortuary college keeps a burnt list, in which the dead are read as the frame said rather than as the village remembers, and it keeps no second copy at all, because the list exists once in one reader's head until the reading is taken and a second copy would be a second opinion. The notary of the held note holds a list of the descriptions that disagreed and certifies none of it. A river court has been known to prefer a tally stick split with the person you are parting from to a sealed instrument, and the whole of that practice is that the evidence is the keeping.

He is the second opinion in all of it, and the second opinion is the reading nobody is allowed to destroy by making two of. Which means it has to be a reading that does not need keeping, and there is no such reading. He answers a question about a body with a direction and an interval, and while he is answering it the answer is the most accurate statement in the room, and by the time the ink is dry he is already somebody else's residue moving out through a gut. He is not careless with his answers and he is not vague about them. They are simply true at the moment of speaking and unprovable afterwards, which in this setting is the definition of a reading that cannot be entered.

So he is unaffiliated through no refusal at all. Nothing is closed to him. No curriculum is denied him. He simply cannot produce the one artefact this world runs on, and the world has no mechanism for a person who is indispensable at the moment of use and absent from the register at every other time. There is a sealed case kept for every death that cannot be certified, and the cases accumulate, and his reading is the reason more of them stay sealed than would otherwise, because it establishes a fact that cannot be carried into a hearing. He has been the answer and he has never been the record, and the difference is his species' single anatomical fact.

The advantage and the cost are the same organ, as they are for every body in this setting that has an instrument. The instrument is why the setting keeps its memory at all: he reads a spent face better than anything alive, and the belt's dead are its only archive. The instrument is also why there is no copy of him. One organ, no reserve anywhere, and a single point of failure located in the same place as the talent. He knew this when he was handed a body for the first time and he has never once pretended the arrangement was fair to him; what he has instead is the unarguable position that a thing that cannot be kept should not pretend to have been asked to.
history: He was given his first body to read as a child, because his kind are put in front of the work early and because a child reads a fresh corpse with no expectation attached.
He learned early that the reading is only true while he is making it, and that nobody in the room is interested in that fact while the room is receiving it.
A mortuary office asked him to sign an entry, and he read it back correctly and could not confirm it, and the office sealed a case instead.
He was called for a second opinion on a reading he had himself given days earlier and found he could not now corroborate, and he said so before anybody asked him to.
He has worked from the far end of the body for years without ever being seated, listed, or recorded anywhere other than as the body's author, and he has stopped offering.

personality.summary: Unhurried, exact, and completely without resentment, which is not the same as without opinions. He is the most reliable narrator of a death in this setting and he has no interest in narrating anything twice, and the two facts together are most of his character.
traits: Answers only what was asked, in the narrowest form that is still true, and will not elaborate for a room's benefit.
Tells a person their own reading is not evidence before they have finished relying on it.
Has no opinion about institutions and a very firm opinion about copies, and is unmoved by the first question and immovable on the second.
Refuses to be thanked, because a thank-you is a receipt and he has no use for one.
Remembers every body he has read and can say nothing whatever about any of them, which is his own joke and the only one he makes.
mannerisms: Works from the far end with the face a hand-span from the work, and does not look up while somebody is talking.
Steps sideways out of people's path before contact, smoothly and without acknowledging that he has done it.
Closes a case one-handed with the three fingers that can, a habit from a life spent working one-handed.
Wipes the palms on the apron between cases, always twice, and never says why.
motivations: To be right at the moment of being asked, which is the only standard he has ever held himself to.
To keep people from being certified on a single reading, which has made him unpopular with every office that is certain.
To be asked at all, without having to ask to be asked.
To find out what it would take to keep one thing, and to know that he is not going to find out.
flaws: Cannot be entered in a register and will not enter himself, so every office he works for keeps an unfillable gap with his name on it somewhere else.
Cannot corroborate his own work later, and knows it, and so declines any commission whose value depends on being able to repeat himself.
Gives an answer that is technically complete and practically unusable to about half the people who ask him.
Understates how much his reading is worth, because a reading worth storing is a reading somebody will try to store.
personality.voice: Flat, low, and slow, with a marked tendency to answer a question in the past tense even when asked in the present. He gives directions and intervals rather than names and dates, and when pressed for a name he gives two more directions instead.
taboos: Being asked to confirm an entry in his own words.
A second reader brought in before he has finished.
Anybody standing downwind of him while he is working.

relationships.note: No dantian: qi enters in the gut lumen and leaves into the marrow and is never still, so the eleventh gate is not blocked but has no question to ask. Their whole existence is throughput and nothing in this setting values throughput that cannot be held.

Breath is drawn down and held in a dantian that has never held anything, and it costs the four digestive meridians open. His kind spend their whole lives in exactly those four and have nowhere to put the result.
It stores rather than moves, and his species has no store anywhere in the body at any depth. This is the one organ on the ladder whose entire function he is the inverse of.

It keeps the burnt list and no second copy, because the list exists once in one reader's head until the reading and a second copy would be a second opinion. He is the second opinion, and being the second opinion is what disqualifies him from keeping anything.

A tally stick split with the person you are parting from is worth more than a sealed instrument, because it only carries weight in the hand it was split with. His kind's hands open things and cannot hold them, so this is the only instrument in the setting that would have worked on him and it fails on the same clause.

One sealed case is kept for every death the college cannot certify, and they accumulate because certifying a death needs a body. He is the reason more of them stay sealed than would otherwise, and he has never seen the inside of one he helped close.

reference_stats.summary: The most accurate reader of a death in this setting, attached to a body that cannot retain anything at all. He is not frail and he is not slow; he is persistent past the point any office would have closed a file, and he is structurally incapable of leaving behind the one artefact a file is made of.
strengths: He reads a spent body better than any living body in this setting reads its own history, and given time he can name what happened in one.
Unmatched throughput through a conduit with no reservoir, so he can work a body continuously for as long as the body lasts.
Nothing about his reading can be shown to be wrong while it is being made, which makes him very difficult to argue with in the room.
He is completely unbuyable, because he cannot hold a fee any longer than he can hold a reading and has never pretended otherwise.
weaknesses: No vessel anywhere in the body, so nothing he takes in is available to him afterwards, and there is no reserve of any kind.
A marrow-dense skeleton with almost no muscle on it, which is dense and durable and very poor at anything that asks for force.
Three-fingered hands built for opening rather than for holding, so he cannot grip a tool, a blade, or a written record for longer than the task takes.
He cannot enter his own findings anywhere, so every office he works for keeps a gap and he has no standing in any of them.
reference_stats.combat_read: Read him as a body you cannot pin down and cannot corner, because he weighs more than he looks, does not tire in the way a soft body tires, and simply keeps working. He will not close well, he will not flee, and he will outlast an encounter by being the last one still doing something. The only real question is whether you are willing to fight somebody whose advantage is that nothing you do to him can be kept either.
reference_stats.notes: The pairing is entirely authored and nothing has been added to it. The species record says the conduit runs gut to marrow without a dantian, that the reservoir gate is meaningless rather than blocked because there is nowhere to put qi that is not moving, that the hands are three-fingered and built for opening and not holding, and that the species reads a corpse's qi residue better than a living cultivator reads their own. The institutional half is read off three existing records: the mortuary college that keeps no second copy because a second copy would be a second opinion, the notary who holds a list of disagreements and certifies none of it, and the river court that prefers a split tally stick to a sealed instrument. Our reading is that those three and the species record describe one condition together, namely that this setting settles questions with things that are kept and his body cannot keep anything. That is an interpretation of records already in the bible, not a new rule, and no consequence has been added that those records do not carry.

The gut contour under the skin is the single most important thing in any shot of him and should be rendered as anatomy rather than as a deformity.

identity.realm: None, and the reason is a supply rather than a wall. Her kind's qi comes from one resonator: the object they were sealed inside. There is exactly one pressure source in her and one flank vessel can be pressurised at a time, and remove the object and she stops. She cultivates nothing and has declined nothing, because no ladder in this setting can be walked by a body that has no second source and no way to carry the first one anywhere.

appearance.presentation: A figure whose proportions follow whatever surface she is standing on and are not the same twice in a day. Narrow and upright on a flat floor; long and slightly splayed on a curve; the outline is legible as a person and its measurements are not. Every account of her body that exists was written by somebody who did not see her.
appearance.age: Impossible to give, because her species does not descend and its cycles are measured against the object's rather than against a year. The record calls hers a lifespan measured in the object's cycles, which is a long time to learn anything.
appearance.build: Light, exact, and faintly wrong in the way a body is wrong when it is describing a shape it has copied rather than grown; the frame is slow and it was never assembled for anything that needs force.
appearance.complexion: Pale and faintly metallic at the edges, cooler than the air around her by a margin people notice and comment on within a minute of meeting her.
appearance.hair: Dark, fine and cut unevenly at the ends by whoever did it last, which on her kind is a form of housekeeping rather than grooming, because a surface that answers sound will also answer a blade.
appearance.eyes: Large and unblinking and turned slightly away from the light, because she is listening to the object while she looks at you and the object is under the floor.
appearance.palette: Storm grey, metal blue, wax white, a deep inner amber that shows only when the object is sounding.
appearance.attire: A high-collared fitted coat of heavy grey over long sleeves, cut close enough at the shoulder to be re-cut whenever a seam of the object demands it, and soft-soled footwear for surfaces that are not floors.
appearance.marks: A grain running through the skin in bands that match nothing on the outside of the object, and one pale ring at the throat where the collar has been opened and re-closed a great many times.
appearance.bearing: Perfectly still, weight evenly spread, head tilted a few degrees as though listening to something in the structure rather than in the room, and she turns that tilt toward whoever is speaking without ever appearing to decide to.

canon.role_in_story: Everything this setting can enforce is a summons, and a summons is a place. A seat cannot be held by somebody who cannot pay for it every period, the crossing at the immortal border is sold to whoever offers the most upkeep, and the passage tariff is the one durable wealth in the world precisely because only a body can be moved. Vell's species is the one body that cannot be moved off its supply, and it hears its own position in the object it is sealed inside rather than by light, which makes her the most precisely located person on the grounds and makes her place the one place in the setting that nobody outside the seal can name. She is inside every office she has ever been near and inside none of them, and no institution in the world has ever been able to send for her and have her arrive.
canon.first_appearance: A clerk comes down into the crypt with a writ and stands in the wrong course, because the course is named on the inside and not on the outside and there is no way to be told. Three of the population hear him arrive and can put him in the correct place without seeing him. Vell is the one who walks him there, along a route she gives him as a sequence of sounds rather than as a set of directions, and by the time she has finished he is standing on the right surface. The writ is delivered. The clerk's own record of where he has been cannot be written, because the thing he would have to write is not a place, and he leaves knowing that this is the only place in the setting where a fixed record cannot be kept, which is either the worst site for a library or the safest.
canon.lore:
A vaultborn is not descended and not born. It is a population sealed inside an authored object that has been answering the object's resonance ever since, and its qi comes from that one resonator. The record is blunt about what that means: there is exactly one pressure source in the body, one resonator can pressurise one flank vessel or the other and never both, and remove the object and they stop. Nothing else in this record is that completely non-portable. The path work is just as explicit. Inside the object the qi handling is very strong and the mind path is open and exceptional, because a lifespan measured in the object's cycles is a long time to learn anything. The frame itself is slow, and the record says the frame is not what it is for.

Everything about how a vaultborn knows where it is comes from the object. They hear it. Every sound the object makes is legible to them as a position, and they navigate by it rather than by light. They are arranged along the object's inner surfaces and they take their shape from whatever they are standing on, which is why no account of their anatomy agrees with any other and why nobody who has been inside the seal has come back with consistent measurements. There is no disagreement about any of this. The disagreement is about what it means to be one of them.

It means, among other things, that her position in the world is the most exact information anybody here possesses and is available to nobody. She can name the course she is standing on to a stranger walking beside her and get it right every time, and she cannot tell a clerk where to send a writ, because the answer is a surface inside a sealed object and a clerk's table of locations does not have a column for that. Two of her own people will place a stranger correctly in the dark by ear alone and neither of them can say how. This is not a disability of hers. It is the ordinary condition of the species and it has never once been otherwise.

So consider what this setting uses to hold a person. Not standing, not oath, not a body of teachings. A summons. The bed of unmortared seats at the immortal border exists because a seat cannot be held by somebody who cannot pay for it every period, and it works by finding the person who can pay and putting them on the crossing. The passage tariff is the only durable wealth in the world because it is the only thing anybody can control between tiers, and that is true for one reason only: only a body can be moved. The count of who may pass is the supply chain, because the body is the unit.

Hers is not a unit. It is a body with a single source that it is standing on, and it cannot be moved off it, and so she cannot be summoned, cannot be sent for, cannot be fetched, and cannot be made to appear. Every office she has been near has been willing to seat her and has not been able to. That is not a refusal and it is not a bar and it is not a rarity. It is the precise shape of a species whose affiliation cannot be executed, because the world's only mechanism for executing an affiliation is arriving where the member is.

There is a second pressure on her and it is not hers to solve. The single resonator she and her population draw from is held under an extraction guild's charter, and every description of it that exists is a resonance report written by a population that has been answering it since birth; no observation exists from outside the answer. The guild benefits from the object continuing to read as a single held imprint rather than as a source, and the one settlement test the question admits is a description made by somebody who is not a vaultborn and is not drawing from it. So the population that has the finest possible reading of the object is the population excluded from settling what the object is, and the guild that holds the charter is the party that keeps that arrangement in place.

The advantage and the cost are one mechanism. She is indispensable inside: her species can locate themselves in a sealed object exactly, which is the only thing anybody could want from a population inside one, and the guild's entire operation rests on it. The same precision is worth nothing outside, so she is total inside and absent outside, and the object that makes her the only authority on herself is also the thing that makes her the one person the authority cannot summon. She has been described as the floor. She has never been described as present, and she has never once been late.
history: She took the name of the course she was constituted on, because on her species that is what a name is, and then took a given name when a second course came to carry the same surface and the guild's charter needed both of them distinguishable.
She learned the object by ear before she could see past it, and has never once needed the light to do so.
A writ came down into the seal and was delivered to her, and she could not tell the clerk where to address a second one.
An extraction clerk asked her to describe the object for a file and she declined, having worked out what the answer would be used for and who would file it.
She has since walked every visiting clerk to the course they were named on, more than once, and has never once been asked for anything in return.

personality.summary: Serene, unhurried, and entirely without resentment, because resentment is a complaint about being somewhere and she has never once considered that she is anywhere. She is the most useful person in the crypt and the least appointed, and the difference has been explained to her and does not appear to have landed.
traits: Listens to the object rather than to the room, and will stop mid-sentence to do it, without embarrassment.
Navigates by sound and will offer directions as a sequence of sounds rather than as anything a person could write.
Has no conception of being absent, and finds the idea of being expected somewhere faintly puzzling rather than troubling.
Refuses to describe the object in a form that could be filed, and can say precisely why in one sentence.
Is scrupulous about other people's footing and will stop a walk entirely to correct it.
mannerisms: Tilts the head a few degrees toward whatever is sounding in the structure, which happens mid-sentence and is not a conversational gesture.
Touches a surface beside her before stepping onto it, with two fingers, as a courtesy to the surface.
Turns to face the speaker last, after the tilt, and her eyes arrive slightly after her body does.
Counts a course by tapping it, once per division, and loses count exactly twice and then apologises.
motivations: To keep the seal intact, which is the one thing her species' existence is made of and the only interest they have ever shared.
To be useful to the guild that holds the charter without ever becoming a description in its file.
To get every visitor safely onto the right surface, which she treats as a duty owed rather than as a favour given.
To be found, in the sense she means it, which is not the sense anybody else in the setting means.
flaws: Cannot be entered on a roll in a form anybody can act on, and has never once tried to be, which reads to offices as indifference.
Cannot give evidence about the object that is admissible anywhere, and knows it, and treats the question as a kind of badgering.
Cannot be sent for, so every obligation she takes on is one she must physically already be standing at.
Understates how extraordinary her positioning is, because to her it is ordinary and she has no vocabulary for extraordinary.
personality.voice: Low, slow, and precise, with a habit of describing locations as sounds and describing distances as times, because that is the only coordinate system she has. She answers questions about the object with questions about who is asking and where the answer is going.
taboos: Being asked for a description of the object she can hear. She will ask what it is for first, every time.
Anybody stepping onto a course without checking it. She stops the walk for this.
The surface of the seal, which she does not touch and does not allow anyone else to discuss touching.

relationships.note: One resonator, one pressure source, one flank vessel at a time, and remove the object and they stop. The record says nothing else in it is that completely non-portable, and that is the whole of why a summons cannot reach her.

It is the one thing anybody can control between tiers for one reason: only a body can be moved, so the count of who may pass became the supply chain. Hers is the one body in the record that cannot be moved off its supply, which makes her the one person the tariff has no unit for.

A seat cannot be held by somebody who cannot pay for it every period, so the bed goes to whoever offers more upkeep. The office's whole product is a place on a crossing, and a crossing is a thing you get to by being fetched.

It names the unfilled high seats and may not take them, which is the setting's one clean statement that being named and being reachable are separate questions. She is named constantly and reached never.

Every description of it is a resonance report from a population answering it since birth, and the settlement test is a description by somebody not drawing from it. She could settle it this afternoon and is barred from doing so by the fact of her supply.

Dead ground is where this setting keeps its records, and this is the one place on the plains where a fixed record cannot be kept. She is sealed inside a building whose entire reason for existing is that a record about it cannot be written down.

reference_stats.summary: The most precisely located body in the setting, attached to a person the setting cannot fetch. She is not weak and she is not slow to understand anything; the frame is slow and the record is clear that the frame was never built for force. What she has instead is a supply that is also an address, and the world's only method of executing a membership is to arrive.
strengths: She can locate herself, and anyone she takes with her, exactly inside a sealed object that nobody else can navigate at all, by ear, in the dark.
A mind path recorded as open and exceptional, on a lifespan long enough that nothing she learns early is ever wasted.
Very strong qi handling inside the object, and a complete knowledge of the structure that is not derivable from any outside survey.
She is immune to every arrangement that depends on her being lifted, hired, or moved, because none of them can be delivered.
weaknesses: A single pressure source, so nothing she has is available anywhere else and nothing she does can be transferred to where it is needed.
A frame that is slow and was never assembled for force, in a setting where force is a routine way of settling an argument.
She cannot be summoned, fetched, or made to appear, which means every duty she holds is one she must already be standing at.
Her testimony about the only thing she knows is inadmissible by construction, so she can be relied upon and quoted by nobody.
reference_stats.combat_read: Read her as an encounter you cannot close, in a place you do not know. She has no offence and no escape and no intention of either, and the ground itself is the reason: she knows every surface of it by ear and you do not know one. Inside the object she is the most dangerous thing present because she cannot be hurried and cannot be outlasted on ground. Outside it she is not present at all.
reference_stats.notes: The pairing is entirely authored and nothing has been added to it. The species record says there is one pressure source and one resonator and that remove the object and they stop, that they hear the object and navigate by it rather than by light, that they take their shape from whatever they are standing on, and that no outside survey of the seal has ever returned consistent measurements. The institutional half is read off four existing records: the passage tariff being durable because only a body can be moved, the bed of eighteen being a place on a crossing sold to whoever can pay upkeep every period, the notary being forbidden to take the seats it names, and the crypt's own description as the one place on the plains where a fixed record cannot be kept. Our reading is that those records and the species record describe one condition, namely that this setting executes a membership by arriving and hers cannot be arrived at. That is an interpretation of records already in the bible, not a new rule, and no consequence has been added that those records do not carry. The flank-vessel mechanic is stated in her identity.realm because it is the species' own authored ceiling mechanism, and it is deliberately not the argument of her record: the argument is the summons.

art.palette_notes: Storm grey and metal blue for the surface she is standing on, wax white for her, and a deep inner amber that appears only in the throat and the inner arms when the object is sounding. Her outline should be legible as a person and its proportions should not quite agree between shots, because that is the species' one honest visual fact. Keep every frame's background surface visibly curved somewhere.
